Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: Feasibility study for NDIS includes civil status data collection/processing; national ID card exists; recent digitalisation efforts mentioned but no fully deployed digital system confirmed; paper-based traditionally with digitization under development.
revision_notes: Original sources (a 2021 press piece on the separate National Digital Identification System feasibility study, and a generic Smile ID KYC country page) did not directly address the state of civil registration digitisation. Fetched both and confirmed neither describes an operational or in-development civil register per se. Searched for fresher, more relevant evidence and found that the Congolese Information Systems Agency (ACSI) has since built the Systeme Integre des Faits d'Etat Civil (SIFEC), a platform to digitalise birth, marriage and death registration and link it to national ID, tax, defence, education and health functions. A three-day validation workshop (18-20 February 2026) finalised 17 technical recommendations on the software, with the principal recommendation being to mobilise the human, material and financial resources still needed to deploy the platform - indicating the system is built and validated but not yet operationally deployed. This supports 'Under development' (3) rather than a higher code; confirmed unchanged with updated, more directly relevant sourcing.
revised_comments: The Republic of Congo is developing a digital civil registration system. The Congolese Information Systems Agency (ACSI) has built the Systeme Integre des Faits d'Etat Civil (SIFEC), a software platform to digitalise birth, marriage and death registration and interlink it with other government functions, including national identification, tax administration, education, health and defence. A February 2026 validation workshop finalised the technical recommendations for the platform, while deployment - including allocation of the necessary human, material and financial resources - remains outstanding. The civil register therefore remains under development rather than fully or partially deployed nationwide.

Definition: What proportion of the intended beneficiaries does the register cover?
Comments: <20% coverage based on 60k households vs 6M population proxy.
revision_notes: Fetched the original 2019 World Bank press release, which confirms the Lisungi Social Registry then held records for 'more than 60,000 households' while the project itself reached only about 10,000 households with cash transfers; the cited comparison to a 6 million total-population proxy is a rough denominator rather than a true intended-beneficiary figure, but corroborating and more recent evidence points to the same sub-20% conclusion. A January 2026 report (Depeches de Brazzaville/allAfrica) on RSU flood-preparedness work states that despite being in place since 2015, the RSU 'reste encore insuffisamment approprie et vulgarise' (remains insufficiently taken up and publicised), with expanding its use and interoperability flagged as a 2026 work-plan priority. The National Social Safety Net Programme launched in August 2024 initially targets only 70,000 households/individuals, against roughly 1.48 million households nationally (2023 census) and a poverty rate estimated at roughly two-fifths or more of the population - implying coverage of the intended (poor/vulnerable) population remains well under 20%. A new dedicated RSU headquarters was inaugurated in April 2026 to support expansion, but no updated coverage percentage has been published. Score confirmed at 1 (<20%) with fresher corroborating sources; precise up-to-date coverage figures were not found, so this is not upgraded.
revised_comments: The Registre Social Unique (RSU), Congo's unified social registry underpinning the Lisungi and National Social Safety Net programmes, covers only a small minority of the intended poor and vulnerable population. Official reporting from early 2026 describes the RSU, in place since 2015, as still insufficiently known and used, with expanding its reach and data interoperability identified as a 2026 government priority. The National Social Safety Net Programme launched in 2024 initially targets around 70,000 households and individuals, a small fraction of Congo's approximately 1.48 million households and of the population living below the poverty line. A new dedicated RSU headquarters opened in Brazzaville in April 2026 to support further registration and interoperability, but coverage of the intended beneficiary population remains below 20%.
